newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnamese bank offers shares to foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: Vietnamese bank offers shares to foreign investors.

text.p: Foreign investors have been invited to take a 30 percent stake in Vietnam's Asian Commercial Bank (ACB) by subscribing to a capital increase, the joint-stock bank's deputy director, Huynh Anh Tuan, said on Friday.
Tuan told Reuters that ACB would raise its registered capital to 300 billion dong ($27.27 million) from 70 billion by the end of this year.

He said applications to subscribe to the 90 billion dong on offer to foreign institutions had been received from banks and financial institutions from Japan, South Korea, the United States and Britain.
A shortlist of foreign investors, each restricted to a maximum 10 percent stake, would be submitted to the central bank for a final decision on stock allocation.
ACB will be the third of communist Vietnam's 46 commercial joint-stock banks to sell shares to foreigners.
One of the most successful joint-stock banks, the Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Private Enterprises (VP Bank), led the way last year and was followed by Maritime Bank.

Vietnam, which began reforming its command economy in the late 1980s, created four big state-run commercial banks out of the central State Bank of Vietnam in 1990. They still account for the lion's share of all deposits and loans.
The smaller joint-stock banks, owned by private shareholders, began operations in 1991.
Foreign bankers say some of the joint-stock banks are obvious candidates for listing on the country's first stock exchange, which the government aims to open by the end of the century.
